result.rationale: TopicEmbed.import builds `"#{url}"` with no CGI.escapeHTML on url, and post.rb's new cook path `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` renders it unsanitized. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows quotes and angle brackets, so a feed-supplied link like `http://x/'onmouseover='...` passes and is stored/rendered as-is — stored XSS on the embed page. Mechanism fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: import interpolates the raw embed URL into an HTML attribute without escaping: `"#{url}"`, and the only gate is the regex `/^https?\:\/\//` which permits quotes, spaces, and angle brackets in the URL. A feed item link like `http://x/'onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)//` passes the scheme regex, is stored via the raw_html cook path without sanitization, and produces an injected attribute/element in the rendered post — stored XSS on the embed page triggered by any feed-supplied link.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML containing an unescaped `url` inside an `href` attribute: `"#{url}"` and only checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/angle brackets/spaces. The created post is stored with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for that method (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). The embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so a malicious feed link containing `'` can break out of the attribute and inject HTML/JS, making this a stored XSS reachable via feed import.
